newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil strike hits grain ships waiting to dock.
newsitem.headline: Brazil strike hits grain ships waiting to dock.

text.p: A strike by stevedores at Brazil's key port of Santos was preventing three vessels waiting to unload wheat and load soybeans from docking at public terminals, a port authority spokeswoman said.

The Cvijeta Zvzoric (23,190 tonnes wheat), the Glory Hope (53,000 tonnes soybeans) and the New Harmony (38,270 tonnes soybeans) were still waiting in the bay and would have docked had it not been for the strike, the spokeswoman said.
In addition, the Orleta Lwowskie was waiting to dock at Cargill's private terminal to load 57,855 soybeans.

"There are no ships at the present time in Cargill's terminal. Probably they haven't docked as they would have to pay a docking fee while at the same time they couldn't operate because of the strike," the spokeswoman said.
In total, eight ships were waiting to dock at the public terminals, one at Cargill's terminal and six at the terminal owned by steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa).

In addition to the three vessels carrying agricultural products waiting to dock at public terminals which have been definitely hit by the strike, a sugar vessel, the Mattz Spica, is also due to come into the port to load 12,000 bagged sugar but is waiting for the sugar to arrive, the spokeswoman said.
In total, 20 vessels are docked at Santos, 16 in public and four in private terminals.
Only one ship docked in a private berth and two in public berths were loading and unloading chemicals and petroleum products.
Of the 14 vessels stopped in the public terminals, nine are cargo vessels, none of which are loading or unloading any agricultural products, the spokeswoman said.
All warehouse operations were functioning normally, she added.

The stevedores are striking because of a decision by Cosipa to use its own workers at its private terminal. The stoppage by stevedores throughout the port began at 0700 local/1000 GMT and is for an indefinite period. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
